tom-customer: Hey team, customers are hitting intermittent 429s for our upload endpoint since ~09:02 UTC. Seen across multiple regions. Sample response headers attached below and a short timeline. Can you advise what to gather?

jess-support: Sorry about that, Tom. Can you paste one full raw response (headers + body) and a single request curl so we can repro locally? Also include any x-request-id from the response.

tom-customer: Sure, here's one response we captured at 2027-05-12T09:02:15Z:
HTTP/2 429
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: 94f2a1b3-cc9e-4d5d-9f7b-8a7c1d0e2f12
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1817543280
retry-after: 60

{"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}

And our app logs show a burst of requests from a single client key between 09:01:50-09:02:30 (approx 160 requests/min).

jess-support: Perfect, thanks. Two quick asks to make triage faster: 1) please run a curl -v to capture full response headers and body and paste output, 2) export a HAR from your browser or capture a tcpdump/proxy access log covering the 09:01:30-09:03:00 window. If you can't share the key, redact it and share the x-request-id.

sara-se: Example repro curl we use for customers — replace $KEY and redact before posting:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload' 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"filename":"small.png","content":"<base64>"}' 
  -v 
  --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt
```

Send /tmp/curl-trace.txt. --trace-ascii gives raw wire headers + timing which helps.

tom-customer: Ok running that now. One more thing: responses also had a second header set: x-quota-window=60s and x-client-burst=40. Not sure if that's from our gateway or yours.

jess-support: Thanks — that suggests a short per-minute burst window is hitting. If you can include the full trace we can confirm whether your client is batching/retrying aggressively. Also share the exact client IP range and token prefix. If you prefer security, upload logs to the secure support upload link and paste the upload id.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2027-1457 — assigned to @amit-oncall.

amit-oncall: I'm pulling gateway logs for the x-request-id 94f2a1b3-cc9e-4d5d-9f7b-8a7c1d0e2f12 and the 09:01:00-09:05:00 window. Quick check: can you confirm if you have multiple threads/processes sharing the same API key? That often causes burst spikes.

tom-customer: Yes, our worker autoscaler kicked up 6 instances within that minute due to a separate processing backlog. We thought throughput would be fine.

amit-oncall: That explains it. We'll attach the gateway timeline; initial look shows a short spike from us-east-1 with many concurrent connections. I'll paste the relevant gateway excerpt when ready.

jess-support: For our side, please also collect a debug bundle: app logs (with local timestamps), proxy/load-balancer access logs, and your client-side retry logic. If you can, set a temporary rate-limit header on client to backoff faster (exponential backoff).

tom-customer: Uploading curl trace + HAR to secure link now: https://support.redwood.ai/uploads/abc123 (link pasted privately).

amit-oncall: Gateway excerpt (sanitized):
```
2027-05-12T09:02:12.341Z request_id=94f2a1b3 client_ip=3.85.12.44 method=POST path=/v1/upload status=200 latency_ms=24
2027-05-12T09:02:13.112Z request_id=94f2a1b3 client_ip=3.85.12.44 method=POST path=/v1/upload status=429 latency_ms=1 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=1817543280
2027-05-12T09:02:14.987Z request_id=ab12c345 client_ip=3.85.12.44 method=POST path=/v1/upload status=429 latency_ms=2 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=1817543280
```

jess-support: Seeing that, the burst exceeded the per-key burst allowance; x-rate-limit-reset aligns with the 60s window. Two remediation paths: 1) throttle clients to keep sustained rate under the limit, 2) request a temporary burst increase for your key while you roll out scaling changes (need business justification). Which do you want?

tom-customer: We'll throttle on our side and also open a ticket for temporary increase while we adjust autoscaling.

jess-support: Great. I'll keep INC-2027-1457 open and attach the debug bundle when the upload completes. If you can, in your next message include the exact curl-trace.txt and the HAR id. That'll let the infra team confirm the reset timing and whether any retries amplified the burst. :thumbsup:
